## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), and each proposed Schur family has \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6, lines 18-42]
- [computed] For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(27\) basis elements and \(327\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(25\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]
- [computed] For rectangular data \((r,q,i,j)=(5,2,1,1)\), the LR presentation has \(20\) basis elements and \(179\) relation vectors; its computed SNF has \(18\) unit factors and no nonunit factors, so \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^2\). [artifact bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f]
- [proved] In both cases \(a=b=1\), hence \(N=2\), and the two candidate families specialize to \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(2)}\}\) and \(\{s_{(1)},s_{(1,1)}\}\). Conditional on the established generation theorem and the two computed cokernels, each family is irredundant: deletion would make \(\mathbb Z^2\) cyclic, which is impossible.
- [unsupported] These computations concern rectangular Schur-data only; no permutation \(v_{r,s,t,n}\) admissibility is asserted.

## Strategy
Construct the integral LR multiplication presentation of \(Q=J/\Lambda_+J\), enumerate all partitions in \(\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\), and compute SNF of the resulting relation matrix. The two tests extend separately beyond the reported ranges \(r\le4\) and \(q=n-r\le5\). [source-6, lines 46-54]

## Gaps
- No independent rerun or reviewer validation of artifact `bfbfd736e27f1a193b24aab07cfae4f512c6c9dd5039963e396331b46516f16f` is supplied.
- Finite computations do not establish the general conjecture or permutation admissibility.

## Next
Independently reproduce both SNF computations with a separate LR/SNF implementation, then obtain grounded \((r,q,i,j)\leftrightarrow v_{r,s,t,n}\) admissibility conditions.
